themes_detail.label: Traffic Crisis Emerges
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints spiked to 8 complaints this week versus a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 482% increase with z-score of 5.96—signaling a sudden, acute street management problem in Crown Heights that emerged THIS WEEK and demands immediate investigation.
evidence: 8 traffic complaints filed last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (482% spike)
Z-score of 5.96 indicates statistically exceptional deviation with high severity rating
This week's spike is the most recent and sharpest anomaly in the dataset
reporting_angles: What triggered this week's traffic surge? Road closures, construction, special events, or transit disruptions?
Are residents reporting specific corridors (Atlantic Ave, Nostrand Ave, Flatbush Ave) as problem zones?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 46 filings last week from a baseline of 20.8 per week—a 122% spike with z-score of 4.49—suggesting new venues, construction, or nightlife activity disrupting residential areas THIS WEEK.
evidence: 46 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 20.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (122% increase)
Z-score of 4.49 indicates high severity statistical anomaly
Residential noise complaints (1,153 total over 90 days) already high; commercial spike adds pressure
reporting_angles: Which commercial establishments or venues are generating complaints? New bars, restaurants, clubs, or construction sites?
Are SLA-licensed venues complying with noise ordinances, and is NYPD responding to complaints?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion in District
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints soared to 12 filings last week from a baseline of 2.5 per week—a 380% spike with z-score of 4.48—indicating a sudden surge in vandalism or gang activity THIS WEEK across Crown Heights.
evidence: 12 graffiti complaints filed last week vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
Z-score of 4.48 flags this as high-severity anomaly
Spike emerged THIS WEEK, most recent after traffic and commercial noise
reporting_angles: Is this coordinated tagging, gang signaling, or general vandalism? Are there identifiable patterns or crew tags?
What areas of Crown Heights/Prospect Heights are most affected? Is Parks or Sanitation responding with cleanup?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 19 filings last week from a baseline of 6.2 per week—a 204% increase with z-score of 3.99—reflecting escalating complaints about Uber, Lyft, or unlicensed car services THIS WEEK.
evidence: 19 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 6.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (204% increase)
Z-score of 3.99 indicates high statistical severity
Converges with traffic spike (both transit-related) THIS WEEK
reporting_angles: Are drivers congesting residential streets? Double-parking? Blocking driveways or bike lanes?
Is there a specific app or service generating complaints? Are they operating in compliance with NYC TLC regulations?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Spreading
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints rose to 93 filings last week from a baseline of 53.2 per week—a 75% spike with z-score of 3.61—indicating worsening garbage management, rodent activity, or street cleanliness THIS WEEK across the district.
evidence: 93 unsanitary condition complaints last week vs. 53.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (75% spike)
Z-score of 3.61 flags as high-severity anomaly
Unsanitary conditions are already the 4th-highest complaint category overall (777 in 90 days); spike THIS WEEK suggests acceleration
reporting_angles: Is Sanitation falling behind on collection schedules? Are there specific blocks or neighborhoods with rodent infestations?
Has there been staffing cuts, strikes, or service disruptions affecting waste pickup?
